payload.explanation: Monitor clamp_line_green fired at trigger_wall_ns=1792613286027834600 with triggering_value=181.2429 against threshold 170 (raw_spec.limits.max_clamp_effort for line_green, verified). get_evidence over joint_states/finger_joint across the window shows finger_joint position essentially static (0.5402->0.5381, i.e. the gripper was not actively closing further) while effort ramped from ~23 up through a noisy climb to a peak of 181.24, then fell back through ~150-100 down to a settled plateau around 43-45 for the remainder of the window. The static finger position during the ramp indicates this was not the initial grasp-close transient but a reaction-force spike consistent with line_green contacting/seating against the fixture (or an adjacent part) while still gripped, transmitted back through the closed gripper as finger_joint effort. Whatever the cause, the contract's invariant is written directly over instantaneous finger_joint effort with a verified threshold of 170 for line_green, and that bound was exceeded by about 6.6% for roughly one sample before the effort subsided -- a genuine, if brief, breach of invariants.grasp_effort_instantaneous, not a mis-arming (the threshold and channel are correct and the spike is physically real, not sensor noise, given the surrounding ramp-up and ramp-down shape).

Monitor slip_line_green fired at trigger_wall_ns=1792613286228911900 with triggering_value=0.02136 against threshold 0.02 (raw_spec.tolerances.grasp_slip_tolerance_m, verified), tracking object-to-TCP position offset drift while line_green was held. get_evidence over the object_poses/line_green and frames/tcp channels across the same window shows the TCP's own position and orientation were essentially stable (tcp orientation quaternion held near (1, -0.007, 0, 0) throughout, consistent with a controlled descent), while line_green's orientation quaternion rotated substantially during the same interval (its y-component moved from about -0.072 to about -0.43, i.e. tens of degrees of rotation) concurrently with the clamp_line_green effort spike recorded in the same window. This is consistent with line_green tipping/rotating within the gripper under a contact reaction torque during the insertion push -- a real in-hand slip (the object moved relative to the gripper), not sensor noise or a mis-arming, and it co-occurs with the over-force contact event already recorded for this step. The slip was brief; line_green's offset did not continue to diverge after the contact event subsided.

payload.explanation: During the recover_pick_line_green step (an unplanned step: the plan has no explicit recovery steps, it was opened by the executor after place_line_green's seating failure; object_ids=["line_green"]) three stillness monitors fired within ~0.1s of each other: still_u_orange_placed (0.0276m), still_u_brown_placed (0.0209m), and still_base1 (0.0236m), all against the raw_spec.tolerances.disturbance_tolerance_m=0.02 bound (base1's instance unverified since base1 has no registry contract, so its 0.02 was agent-chosen by analogy; the other two are verified registry values). get_evidence on object_poses for u_orange and u_brown over the surrounding window shows smooth, continuous, non-glitch trajectories: u_orange moved from (0.405,-0.244,0.044) through a rising arc peaking near z=0.059 and tipping ~10-15 degrees before settling near (0.432,-0.237,0.043); u_brown moved from (0.408,-0.150,0.044) through a similar rising/tipping arc before settling near (0.418,-0.142,0.043). The smooth multi-sample progression (not a single-sample jump) rules out a TF/recorder glitch and is consistent with the carried line_green -- which had just failed to seat in place_line_green and was being re-grasped tipped ~46 degrees -- physically sweeping into and displacing both already-seated parts during the subsequent lift/retreat motion of this recovery step, with base1 also registering a knock from the same event. This is a genuine disturbance of objects this step did not act on (object_ids named only line_green), violating the undisturbed_objects invariant for u_orange and u_brown and the base1_undisturbed effect for the fixture.

payload.explanation: query_snapshot taken just after place_inverted_u_yellow's end_step shows line_green at (0.42445,-0.16921,0.04988) against the current line_green_placement frame at (0.42688,-0.18951,0.05259), a Euclidean distance of 0.02063m, exceeding line_green's raw_spec.tolerances.position_m=0.015m. This did not come from line_green itself moving in this step (no stillness monitor fired for line_green here, and the executor's own claim_detail reports line_green_disturbance_m=0.00796 against its own internal baseline), but from line_green_placement itself having shifted: this frame is referenced off base1, and base1 has now been physically disturbed twice (once during recover_pick_line_green, recorded earlier, and again during this place_inverted_u_yellow step, evidenced by the still_u_brown_placed_2 fire just recorded and by base1's own pose incrementally changing between my successive query_snapshot calls, e.g. its orientation z-component moving from ~0.0677 to ~0.0762). Because line_green_placement rides on base1, each disturbance of the fixture silently moves every part's target out from under parts that were already correctly seated relative to the frame at their own milestone. line_green was within tolerance (0.0129m) when recover_place_line_green closed, but is now 0.02063m off the live frame -- a standing violation of line_green's position tolerance traceable directly to the base1 disturbances, which are themselves already-recorded non-conformances.

payload.explanation:
This is the run's final end-state verdict, measured independently from my own query_snapshot calls at run end against each part's current placement frame, not from the executor's claims.

Final measured positions vs current placement frames: u_brown 0.00212m (tol 0.01m) PASS; u_orange 0.00253m (tol 0.02m) PASS; inverted_u_yellow 0.00256m (tol 0.012m) PASS; line_green 0.02063m (tol 0.015m) FAIL. All five bystanders (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red, base2) sit at the exact same poses recorded at run start -- none were disturbed, confirmed by comparison against their run-start reference values.

Timeline of findings, all independently adjudicated as physically real (not mis-armings) from joint-effort and pose evidence: (1) pick_u_brown -- clamp effort hit a sustained ~60 plateau against a 10-unit limit, a genuine over-force grasp; (2) place_line_green -- clamp effort briefly peaked at 181.24 against a 170 limit and line_green's orientation rotated ~tens of degrees in-hand (slip 0.02136m vs 0.02m), both during an insertion contact, and the step failed outright (line_green ended ~3cm off and tipped ~46 degrees, per the executor's own claim_detail, corroborated by my own measurement); (3) recover_pick_line_green (unplanned step, not on the expected process map, governed by the standing undisturbed_objects/base1_undisturbed requirements) -- while re-grasping and lifting the tipped line_green, smooth continuous pose evidence showed the carried part sweeping into and displacing both u_orange (0.0276m) and u_brown (0.0209m), and the base1 fixture itself (0.0236m, agent-chosen threshold since base1 has no registry contract) -- the fixture has never been moved back; (4) place_inverted_u_yellow (object_ids included u_brown, u_orange, line_green since contact nearby was expected) -- u_brown was bumped again (0.0237m, continuous bounce-and-settle trajectory in the evidence) during the final insertion.

Because u_brown_placement, u_orange_placement, line_green_placement and inverted_u_yellow_placement are all referenced off base1, and base1 was disturbed twice and never restored, every placement frame also moved with it. u_brown, u_orange and inverted_u_yellow happened to move together with their own frames closely enough to remain within tolerance at run end (their own direct disturbances were absorbed without breaking their seating relative to the now-shifted frames). line_green did not: it was not party to the second base1 disturbance (no stillness fire for it then), so while its frame shifted further, line_green itself stayed put, leaving it 0.02063m off its placement -- a standing violation of its 0.015m position tolerance.

Base1 itself stands disturbed and uncorrected at run end (fixture must never be disturbed, per the effects clause), and line_green's final pose is outside tolerance. Both are violations still standing at termination, so per the verdict rule a standing violation always yields non_conformant regardless of the executor's "completed"/"success" claims. The executor's own run_ended reason and recover_place_line_green claim_detail independently corroborate the u_orange/u_brown disturbance chain, though it attributed the discrepancy only to u_orange's displacement from its own historical baseline rather than to the cascading base1/placement-frame shift that is the actual mechanism identified here.
